newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: PRESS DIGEST - SRI LANKA NEWSPAPERS - AUG 13.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - SRI LANKA NEWSPAPERS - AUG 13.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Sri Lankan political and business stories prepared for Reuters by NewsWatch, Colombo Tel/Fax: 94-1-735182 Internet: lucien@eureka.lk.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
TIGER MANHUNT FOR TWO KEY DESERTERS

The Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) are hunting for two of their senior cadres, who have made off with large sums of money in eastern Sri Lanka. The two rebels were said to be on their way to the northern Wanni region, where government troops are battling LTTE rebels in an attempt to open a strategic highway to Jaffna peninsula, when they disappeared. TORTOISE SMUGGLER HELD IN SRI LANKA

A local businessman was taken into custody at Colombo's international airport while attempting to smuggle 41 rare star tortoises to Germany. The baby tortoises fetch between $500-1,000 in the international market. THREE HELD FOR ATTEMPTING TO BUY HELICOPTOR
Three Colombo businessmen, who were trying to buy a MI24 military attack helicopter illegally, have been arrested by police under emergency regulations.
LANKADEEPA, VIRAKESARI, DINAMINA & THINAKKURAL BUS SERVICES CRIPPLED BY STRIKE

The strike by workers at various bus depots across Sri Lanka has crippled public bus services. Outstations commuters were the worst hit. Transport Minister A.H.M. Fowzie has appealed to the strikers to return to work immediately since the strike would further worsen the already faltering financial situation of these companies. But the general secretary of the All Ceylon Motor Workers Union James Kariyawasam has said the strike will go on until the workers were given a 40 percent salary hike.
SOLUTIONS TO BE FOUND FOR PROBLEMS FACED BY TAMILS

Justice and Constitutional Affairs Minister Gamini Peiris has said that the divide between ethnic communities in Sri Lanka will continue to widen unless solutions to the political and day-to-day problems faced by Tamils were found.
SRI LANKA SPRINTER SAYS AIMING FOR OLYMPIC GOLD

Susanthika Jayasinghe, the 200 meters silver medalist at the World Athletic Championships in Athens, has said she was aiming to win an Olympic gold. Jayasinghe was given a rousing welcome by Sri Lankan, who lined the streets in thousands to watch the new sprint queen return home.
